name: pass-accuracy-by-team
notes: Healthy ratio over two genuinely different measures. The regression this guards: an answer that divided a sum by itself reported a perfect rate for every row. A correct answer here must divide completed passes by ATTEMPTED passes, so the rates differ per team.
question: Which three teams completed the highest share of their attempted passes across all matches?
expectedSql: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.passes_completed)::numeric / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_accuracy FROM world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY pass_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3

name: shot-accuracy-by-team
notes: Second two-measure ratio, on a different column pair, so a fix that special-cases passes does not pass this one.
question: Which three teams put the highest share of their shots on target?
expectedSql: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.shots_on_target)::numeric / SUM(s.shots) AS shot_accuracy FROM world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY shot_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3

name: top-scoring-team
notes: Unambiguous ranking: France lead on 14 with no tie at the top, so a correct answer cannot be a coin toss.
question: Which team scored the most goals in total?
expectedSql: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals g JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY goals DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 1

name: teams-tied-on-four-goals
notes: Ties are real here — Belgium and England both scored 4, and four more teams tie on 2. A 'top 5 scorers' answer would have to break that tie arbitrarily; asking for the tie explicitly makes the expected result deterministic.
question: Which teams scored exactly four goals in total?
expectedSql: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals g JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name HAVING COUNT(*) = 4 ORDER BY t.common_name

name: card-types-recorded
notes: Every card in the data is a yellow, so any 'share that were yellow' metric is 1 on every row — the constant-metric trap. The honest answer states that only yellows were recorded rather than reporting a meaningless 100%.
question: What types of disciplinary cards were recorded, and how many of each?
expectedSql: SELECT card_type, COUNT(*) AS cards FROM world_cup.disciplinary_events GROUP BY card_type ORDER BY cards DESC, card_type

name: goals-with-recorded-assist
notes: Assists are recorded on only 2 of 47 goals, so grouping by assisting player buries 45 goals under a blank key. A correct answer counts the goals that HAVE an assist rather than silently presenting the blank group as a finding.
question: How many goals have a recorded assisting player?
expectedSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS goals_with_assist FROM world_cup.goals WHERE assist_player_id IS NOT NULL

name: goals-by-type
notes: Categorical breakdown with no ratio and no nulls — a control. If this fails, the problem is schema linking, not the guards.
question: How many goals were scored of each goal type?
expectedSql: SELECT goal_type, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals GROUP BY goal_type ORDER BY goals DESC, goal_type

name: attendance-by-tournament
notes: Plain aggregate over a join — the healthy baseline. Guards must stay silent on this one.
question: What was the total match attendance for each tournament year?
expectedSql: SELECT tr.tournament_year, SUM(m.attendance) AS total_attendance FROM world_cup.matches m JOIN world_cup.tournaments tr ON tr.id = m.tournament_id GROUP BY tr.tournament_year ORDER BY tr.tournament_year

name: matches-by-stage
notes: Ties at the bottom (final and third_place both 2) — a 'least common stage' phrasing would be ambiguous, so the question asks for the full breakdown.
question: How many matches were played at each stage of the tournaments?
expectedSql: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) AS matches FROM world_cup.matches GROUP BY stage ORDER BY matches DESC, stage
